hormuzEvents.e: DAY 163 — THE NEGOTIATOR'S CHAIR CHANGES HANDS. President Pezeshkian appointed Mohsen Rezaee secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, replacing Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr, who had issued Iran's six conditions for reopening Hormuz a day earlier and now becomes political adviser to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei. Khamenei separately named Rezaee his representative on the council. Rezaee, 71, commanded the IRGC from 1981 to 1997; he said earlier in August that Iran will never allow an unauthorised route through the strait. Trump told Axios the US is 'low-keying it' and 'only semi-negotiating', content to let economic pressure build. ADNOC reported attacks on three of its vessels transiting the strait. Pezeshkian described Iran's condition as 'neither war nor peace', naming economic hardship rather than military conflict as the country's central problem.

DAY 162 — ROUTES AGREED, STRAIT STILL SHUT. Iran and Oman agreed the coordinates of vessel routes through Hormuz and Araghchi called the talks 'approaching the final stages' — while cautioning it is 'not a sign of the reopening' and that reopening is subject to compensation for the US violation of the June memorandum. Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary Zolghadr said the strait will never fully reopen until the US 'corrects its behaviour', listing six demands: no further threats, end the blockade, withdraw all regional military assets, lift sanctions, unfreeze assets, pay war compensation. An IRGC spokesman called the reopening 'completely independent' of the Oman track. Hours later Iran targeted an ADNOC-owned vessel inside the strait; the UAE blamed Iran. Oman warned that further attacks on shipping could derail the deal.

DAYS 159-161 — TERMS, NOT REOPENING. Iran's parliament reviewed the draft Hormuz shipping law: US and Israeli vessels barred outright; states deemed hostile required to pay compensation before transit; violators fined 20% of cargo value; and full reopening conditional on the US lifting its maritime blockade. Iran's deputy foreign minister said the Oman channel arrangement would not necessarily mean the strait reopens. Explosions were reported near Qeshm Island. Houthi forces claimed attacks on Saudi troop positions. Brent: ~$79 low Tue-Wed, +3%+ Thu, settled $83.55 Fri (+1.3%). DAY 109-111 — MAJOR CORRECTION: THE MOU WAS SIGNED 2 DAYS EARLY, AT VERSAILLES, NOT BURGENSTOCK. Wednesday June 17 evening: President Trump PERSONALLY SIGNED the US-Iran memorandum of understanding during a state dinner at the Palace of Versailles, France (G7 sidelines), with French President Macron standing beside him. IRAN'S PRESIDENT MASOUD PEZESHKIAN also signed in person — distinct from the earlier digital signing Sunday Jun 15 by VP Vance and Parliament Speaker Qalibaf. PAKISTAN PM SHEHBAZ SHARIF confirmed: 'Islamabad MoU shall enter into force with immediate effect and, as a first step, the Islamic Republic of Iran will instantly reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and the United States of America will immediately lift the naval blockade.' Sharif praised both Khamenei and Pezeshkian for 'wisdom, foresight and statesmanship.' THE TRUMP ADMINISTRATION REVEALED THE 14-POINT MOU IN FULL Wednesday: (1) Immediate/permanent end to war on all fronts including Lebanon. (2) Mutual sovereignty respect, non-interference. (3) Hormuz: Iran's lead negotiator Ghalibaf said the strait 'will NOT return to pre-war conditions' — Iran will 'receive a fee for services' to shipping, meaning the PGSA toll framework persists in modified form. (4) Nuclear: Iran 'reaffirms it shall not procure or develop nuclear weapons'; enriched uranium to be 'down-blended on site under the supervision of the IAEA' via a mechanism still to be 'mutually agreed.' (5) $300 BILLION FUND DENIED: Trump — 'not investing 10 cents' — the deal instead permits THIRD-PARTY investment into Iran contingent on compliance, not a direct US fund (refuting earlier FT/Iranian-media reports). KHAMENEI AUTHORISED THE DEAL THURSDAY despite holding 'a different view,' after assurances from Pezeshkian that Iran's rights and 'Resistance Front' interests would be protected; Pezeshkian/SNSC pledged not to yield to 'excessive' future US demands. US LAWMAKERS (both parties) flagged concerns: nuclear verification mechanism undefined, Iran's missile programme not addressed. Trump will send the deal to Congress. IAEA DIRECTOR GROSSI: 'It is good that the memorandum is there. Now the technical work starts.' military.t: AUG 9 — IRAN NAMES MOHSEN REZAEE, EX-IRGC COMMANDER-IN-CHIEF, TO ITS TOP SECURITY POST
military.d: President Pezeshkian appointed Rezaee secretary of the Supreme National Security Council on Sunday, replacing Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr, who moves to political adviser to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei; Khamenei also named Rezaee his representative on the council, putting one man at the centre of security decision-making. Rezaee, 71, led the IRGC from 1981 to 1997 and has said Iran will never allow an unauthorised route through Hormuz. Assessment: the official who published the six reopening conditions has been replaced, one day later, by someone with a harder public line on the strait. Read as IRGC consolidation, this lowers the odds of the Oman framework converting into an actual reopening in the near term.

military.t: AUG 9 — TRUMP: US IS 'LOW-KEYING IT', 'ONLY SEMI-NEGOTIATING' WITH TEHRAN
military.d: Speaking to Axios on Sunday, the president said Washington is content to let economic pressure build, describing Iran as being in 'very bad shape' with high inflation and no money. This follows CNN reporting that the chairman of the Joint Chiefs has privately argued the US needs an off-ramp because escalation options could backfire. Assessment: both sides are now signalling willingness to wait. That points to a longer plateau rather than either a deal or an escalation in the next fortnight — and a longer plateau is itself the base case for India's fuel costs.

military.t: AUG 7-8 — MECCA JOINT DEFENCE AGREEMENT: SAUDI ARABIA, PAKISTAN AND TURKEY

India's MEA said New Delhi is 'closely following' the development. Assessment: still the most consequential India-facing development of this war — India's Gulf energy relationships now sit inside a security framework that includes Pakistan. assessment.body:
Monday 8:15 AM IST, pre-open. Day 164. The weekend moved the personnel, not the paperwork.

THE PERSONNEL CHANGE
• Mohsen Rezaee, IRGC commander-in-chief from 1981 to 1997, is now secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, appointed by President Pezeshkian.
• He replaces Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr, who issued the six reopening conditions on Saturday and becomes political adviser to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei.
• Khamenei separately named Rezaee his own representative on the council — both roles in one person.
• Rezaee said earlier this month Iran will never allow an unauthorised route through the strait.
• Observers read the change as the IRGC consolidating control over security decision-making.

THE AMERICAN POSTURE
• Trump told Axios the US is 'low-keying it' and 'only semi-negotiating', content to let economic pressure build.
• This sits alongside reporting that the Joint Chiefs chairman privately wants an off-ramp because escalation options could backfire.
• Reporting also suggests Washington could lift the naval blockade once unrestricted commercial transit resumes — the reciprocal Tehran has not accepted.

ASSESSMENT
• Two capitals signalling patience at the same time is the signature of a plateau, not a turning point.
• The Oman framework and an open strait remain different products. Nothing this weekend moved the second one closer; the personnel change moved it further away.
• For India this argues against both the relief case (Brent back to the $70s on a reopening) and the shock case (a fresh closure spike) over the next fortnight. Plan for $80-86 Brent and a rupee near 95.
• Confidence: high on the appointment and its signalling; moderate on the plateau call; low on timing of any reopening.

INDIA WATCHLIST THIS WEEK
• Today's session — the first read on the six conditions and the Mecca pact together.
• Any fuller MEA statement on the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement beyond 'closely following'.
• Whether ADNOC's tally of attacked vessels rises further, and what it does to Gulf war-risk premiums.
• OMC under-recovery if Brent holds above $85 — the pump-price question returns at that level, not below it.
• FII flows: about $1.3bn bought in August to date is what is holding this two-week rally up.

brief: Day 164, Monday morning before the market opens. Risk to India: high, and the weekend made a near-term Hormuz reopening less likely, not more.

The big change is who Iran has put in charge. On Saturday its national security council listed six conditions for reopening the strait — the US must stop threatening Iran, end the naval blockade, withdraw all its forces from the region, lift sanctions, release frozen money and pay war damages. On Sunday the man who issued that list was moved aside and replaced by Mohsen Rezaee, who ran the Revolutionary Guards for sixteen years and has said Iran will never allow an unapproved route through the strait.

Washington is not rushing either. Trump said the US is 'only semi-negotiating' and is happy to let Iran's economy keep hurting. When both sides are content to wait, the likeliest outcome is not a deal and not a blow-up — it is this, for longer.
Meanwhile Abu Dhabi's national oil company now says three of its ships have been attacked in the strait. So the route paperwork is finished and the water is still dangerous.

For your money: markets open at 9:15 and the early signal is flat — GIFT Nifty around 24,655 against Friday's close of 24,570.65, with Asia firmer but oil capping the upside. Petrol ₹111.21, diesel ₹97.83 and an LPG cylinder ₹942, all unchanged. Nothing is short; the pressure stays on price.
